chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Zurara, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a free man who married a slave woman, and then she was manumitted before he divorced her. He (the Imam) said: 'She has more right to her private part (i.e., the marriage bond remains valid and she is not automatically free/divorced).'

key_terms.أَمْلَكُ بِبُضْعِهَا: She has more right to her private part (marriage bond)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the marriage bond when a free man's slave wife is manumitted before divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *tamlik al-khitah* (marrying a slave woman), establishing that manumission (*itq*) does not automatically dissolve the marital bond. The Imam’s ruling that 'she has more right to her private part' underscores the husband's continued ownership of the conjugal right, distinguishing this status from a free wife where divorce is the sole mechanism for separation. This principle remains central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the legal transition of slave wives upon their freedom.
